newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Welteke says wants stable, stronger dollar.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Welteke says wants stable, stronger dollar.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday that the Bundesbank would welcome a more stable and a stronger dollar.

"We would like to see a more stable dollar," Welteke told journalists in answer to a question. He also said "we would like a stronger dollar," adding that the German export industry would benefit from a stronger U.S. currency.
He declined to give specific levels of where the German central bank would like to see the dollar.
Buba's Welteke says wants stable, stronger dollar
Welteke, who is also president of the state central bank in Hesse, said "naturally we would prefer a less volatile dollar as turbulences in exchange rates are difficult for industry."
Referring to an earlier news agency report that he saw no reason for the dollar to appreciate, Welteke said "we must have misunderstood one another on that point."
"Just as I am unable to explain why the dollar has picked up again, I am equally unable to say why it could fall," he said.
He added that movements of the foreign exchange market are hard to predict and that the market sometimes acts in a contrary fashion to what would be expected from fundamental news.
